First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
